title: Get paid
content:
## What you'll get

Your app can collect payments through Stripe - just describe what you want to charge, paste in two keys, and test with fake cards before going live.

---

## The golden rule: test mode first

Stripe has **two universes**: test mode and live mode. Test mode uses pretend money and fake cards - nothing charges a real bank account. Live mode is real cash.

<Callout type="warning" title="Always start in test mode">
Never use live Stripe keys until you've tested checkout end-to-end with fake cards. One typo in your pricing prompt could accidentally charge real customers the wrong amount.
</Callout>

When you sign up at [stripe.com](https://stripe.com), you'll see test keys (they start with `pk_test_` and `sk_test_`). Use those first.

---

## Step 1: Describe what you want to sell

Tell your Emergent agent exactly what you're charging for. Be specific:

**Good prompts:**
- "Add Stripe payment processing. Users should be able to purchase credits for $10, $25, or $50."
- "Integrate Stripe subscriptions with three tiers: Basic ($9/month), Pro ($29/month), and Enterprise ($99/month)."
- "Add a checkout flow where users can buy individual products from a catalog."

The agent writes all the code - buttons, checkout pages, server logic to confirm payment.

---

## Step 2: Paste your Stripe keys

Once the checkout is built, tell the agent:

```
Set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY to sk_test_xxxxx
Set STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY to pk_test_xxxxx
```

(Replace the `xxxxx` with your actual test keys from the Stripe dashboard.)

<Callout type="note" title="Why two keys?">
The **publishable** key goes in your front-end code (safe to expose). The **secret** key stays on the server (never shown to users). Emergent's environment variable system keeps the secret key hidden.
</Callout>

---

## Step 3: Test with fake cards

Ask the agent to test:

```
Test the Stripe checkout flow
```

The agent will simulate a purchase. You can also manually click your new Buy button and use [Stripe's test card numbers](https://stripe.com/docs/testing) - like `4242 4242 4242 4242` for a successful charge, or `4000 0000 0000 0002` to trigger a card decline.

Watch what happens: does the success page show up? Does your database record the sale?

<Callout type="info" title="Screenshot coming soon">
Screenshot to be added.
</Callout>

---

## Step 4: Switch to real money (when ready)

When everything works in test mode and you're ready to accept real payments:

1. Go to your Stripe dashboard, flip the toggle from **Test** to **Live** mode, and copy your live keys (`pk_live_`, `sk_live_`).
2. Update your environment variables:
   ```
   Set STRIPE_SECRET_KEY to sk_live_xxxxx
   Set STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY to pk_live_xxxxx
   ```
3. Deploy: `Deploy the app with production Stripe keys`

<Callout type="warning" title="Double-check prices">
Before you deploy live keys, re-read your pricing prompts. A typo like "$999/month" instead of "$9.99/month" will charge customers real money at the wrong amount.
</Callout>

---

## When does money reach your bank?

Stripe holds funds for a few days (usually 2-7 business days for your first payouts, then 2 days ongoing) before depositing to your bank account. You set up your bank details in the Stripe dashboard under **Settings → Bank accounts and scheduling**.

The money flows **Stripe → your bank**, not through Emergent. We never touch your revenue.

---

## If something looks wrong

- **Checkout button does nothing**: check the browser console for errors. Your publishable key might be missing or mistyped.
- **Payment succeeds but user doesn't get access**: your webhook might not be set up. Ask the agent: `Set up Stripe webhooks to handle payment confirmation`.
- **Test card declined in test mode**: make sure you're using a [Stripe test card](https://stripe.com/docs/testing), not a real one.
